tier_reason: First-party InfinyOn blog (Feb 11, 2025) with a head-to-head Kafka vs Fluvio producer test on named CPUs (M1 Max, Graviton c7g.xlarge) and exact CLI commands, but no Kafka/Fluvio/JVM/Rust versions, no compiler flags, and no published harness repo beyond the built-in `fluvio benchmark` CLI (crates/fluvio-benchmark), so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Page summary: "1.5 times the throughput and 20 to 38 times better latency" than Kafka at default configs. M1 Max: 76,923 rec/s / 394.6 MB/s / 5.8ms P99 (Fluvio) vs 49,346 rec/s / 240.95 MB/s / 132ms P99 (Kafka); EC2 c7g.xlarge: 37,195 rec/s / 190.8 MB/s / 10.8ms P99 (Fluvio) vs 26,780 rec/s / 130.77 MB/s / 419ms P99 (Kafka). Per machine: 1.56x (M1) and 1.39x (EC2) throughput, 22.8x and 38.8x lower P99 (derived from page data).
corrections.hardware: MacBook Pro 18, Apple M1 Max, 32GB RAM; AWS EC2 c7g.xlarge (ARM64 Graviton, 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM, Elastic Block Storage)
corrections.caveats: First-party vendor (InfinyOn, makers of Fluvio) blog post; Kafka, Fluvio, Java and Rust versions not stated (only 'latest'); no compiler flags or JVM tuning; default configs only; single-node localhost broker; different load generators (kafka-producer-perf-test.sh vs `fluvio benchmark producer`); page mentions 'several trials' until performance stabilized but gives no error bars; no public benchmark repo or CI artifact beyond the built-in fluvio-benchmark crate

notes: All numbers match the page exactly; the page's '1.5x' is its own rounded summary (derived per-machine ratios are 1.56x and 1.39x). The '10-core' detail in hardware is not on the page, so it was removed. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 5,258 stars, last default-branch commit 2026-05-14 (active), not a fork or archived.

tier_reason: First-party author blog post (2018) comparing against Apache Kafka on the same localhost NVMe/XFS host, with exact commands. It does not state the CPU model, compiler or flags, and does not link benchmark code. The smfb benchmark client it ran no longer exists under src/smfb on master. That is C.

corrections.workload: Write 100M 100-byte records via Kafka ProducerPerformance (kafka_2.11-1.0.0, i.e. Kafka 1.0.0; acks=1, lz4 compression.codec=3, 32 partitions) vs the SMF smfb low-level client (batch-size 8196, poll mode, pinned cpusets) against a Seastar-based write-ahead log using O_DIRECT on XFS (epoll + Seastar aio, no DPDK), all on one localhost NVMe/XFS/kernel-4.14 host. Measured end-to-end and server-observed latency; a second workload used 100 messages per batch.
corrections.claimed_speedup: ~48x lower worst-case (slowest) latency than Apache Kafka: page states 'Kafka.Slowest(1618ms) / SMF.Slowest(34ms) ~= 48 lower latency', after a performance-debugging pass. SMF started '-1.3X slower' than Kafka after the rewrite. No throughput comparison figures are given.
corrections.caveats: First-party blog post by the project author (2018); exact CPU model, compiler and flags not stated; localhost-only test (the author notes that network-rack latency is omitted); the headline 48x is max latency only, and the page gives no percentile tables or throughput comparison; old baseline (Kafka 1.0.0 with acks=1); the benchmark client (smfb) is not present on the current master; GitHub SPDX shows NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE file is Apache-2.0; repo abandoned (last default-branch commit 2021-10-17)

notes: The 1618ms vs 34ms slowest-latency numbers and the 1.3x-slower starting point are on the page. The record's workload wording ('100-byte and 8196-message batches', 'Kafka 2.11-1.0') was garbled, so it was rewritten from the page's commands. The last commit was corrected: 2023-04-12 was only a dependabot docs-branch push, and master's last commit is 2021-10-17. Still abandoned. License verified as Apache-2.0 from the LICENSE text.

tier_reason: First-party release post and README tables compare against a single-broker Kafka and RocksDB's WAL. Benchmark code is public (benchmarks/multithreaded_benchmark_writes.rs, benchmarks/multithreaded_benchmark_writes_kafka.java, benchmarks/multithreaded_benchmark_writes_rocksdb.rs), but CPU model, compiler and flags are not stated, so it is C, not A.

corrections.hardware: Not stated in the post or README (CPU model, RAM, storage device and OS version unspecified); Walrus's default fd backend is io_uring-based, implying Linux
corrections.workload: 10-thread sustained write benchmark (Walrus legacy append_for_topic() path using pwrite(), no io_uring batching) against a single Apache Kafka broker (no replication, no networking overhead; Java producer with acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, linger.ms=0, batch.size=16384, 500-1024-byte random payloads, one topic per thread) and RocksDB's WAL. Measured writes/sec and MB/s for unsynced ('no fsync') and fsync'd writes.

notes: All unsynced and synced numbers match the v0.2.0 post and the README tables exactly. The ~8% unsynced edge (1.084x, derived from page data) is modest, and synced writes are a tie, with RocksDB slightly ahead. The Kafka harness confirms 10 threads, acks=all and idempotence; the README confirms single broker, no replication, no network. Metadata checked: MIT, 1,933 stars, last commit 2026-05-13 (active).
